_meta: DEV PLACEHOLDERS — structural world/player/stamina numbers below remain provisional. Hazard/relic/scanner/consumable/throwable balance values are first-pass balanced (see _balanced).
_balanced: 2026-07-05 first-pass balance pass — testable values pending playtesting
_sprint_and_stamina_removed: DELETED 2026-08-01: sprint_speed_mult (1.6), stamina_sprint_cost_per_sec (30.0), stamina_max (100.0), stamina_regen_rate (20.0), stamina_regen_delay (1.0), stamina_recovery_threshold (20.0) — together with the sprint mechanic and the entire Stamina system (src/player/Stamina.gd and its node in Player.tscn). Sprint was Stamina's last consumer once the depth oxygen drain was removed earlier the same day. Movement speed is now base player_move_speed only, modified by the Speed relic, status effects (Dust slow / Bloodstim) and the Tempest armor passive. Do not re-add a sustained self-serve speed boost — it would make the single-use ~3-4s Speed relic worthless.
_hazards_meta: FIRST-PASS BALANCED 2026-07-05 — hazards forgiving early, spike hard toward Inner Core. Testable, pending playtesting.
_pressure_dps_base_meta: FIRST-PASS 2026-07-05 (6.0); HALVED 2026-07-06 (too punishing) 6.0 → 3.0; REDUCED 2026-07-31 (still too high in playtest) 3.0 → 2.0 (-33%); REDUCED AGAIN 2026-08-01 (loiter-time pass) 2.0 → 0.8 (-60%). pressure_dps_base × LAYER_DEPTH_FACTOR (0.0/0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8, LOCKED in Constants) → Crust 0 / Mantle 0.16 / Outer 0.32 / Inner 0.48 / Core Hollow 0.64 per sec (was 0/0.4/0.8/1.2/1.6). REASON for the 2026-08-01 cut: pressure is a CONSTANT, always-on, armor-bypassing tax that starts the moment you enter a layer and never stops — unlike the storm, there is no way to outrun it, so it sets the hard ceiling on how long a player may stay in a layer to loot and fight. Combined with depth_hazard it left only ~19s of life in Inner Core, the layer with the best loot. NOTE: pressure is the ONLY hazard that applies inside the Core Hollow (depth_hazard.core_hollow_dps is 0), so it stacks with the post-17:30 storm to set the finale's time-to-kill — see storm_timings.json _combined_note.

depth_hazard._meta: FIRST-PASS BALANCED 2026-07-05; layer DPS HALVED 2026-07-06; REDUCED 2026-07-31; REDUCED AGAIN 2026-08-01 (loiter-time pass); OXYGEN DRAIN REMOVED 2026-08-01. DPS/visibility scale low Crust / moderate Mantle / noticeable Outer Core / high Inner Core; Core Hollow left to the storm. Testable, pending playtesting.
depth_hazard._balance_note: Layer DPS (depth_hazard only). 2026-07-05 first pass 0/1/4/12/0 → 2026-07-06 halved 0/0.5/2/6/0 → 2026-07-31 reduced 0/0.3/1.3/4/0 → 2026-08-01 REDUCED AGAIN: Crust 0 (unchanged) / Mantle 0.3 → 0.2 (-33%) / Outer Core 1.3 → 0.5 (-62%) / Inner Core 4.0 → 1.0 (-75%) / Core Hollow 0 (unchanged). Shape preserved: 0 at both ends, monotonically increasing Mantle → Inner Core. Visibility alpha deliberately NOT touched — the feedback was about damage. (Oxygen drain was also untouched by the damage passes, then REMOVED outright later the same day — see _oxygen_removed below.) REASON for the deep cuts: depth_hazard was the DOMINANT term deep down (at Inner Core, 4.0 dps here vs 1.2 pressure vs 6.5 storm), so it — not the storm — was what made Outer Core / Inner Core unlootable: 2.1 combined ambient dps at Outer Core and 5.2 at Inner Core meant ~48s and ~19s of life on a full-health player with the storm nowhere near, which is less time than opening a chest. Since Epic and Legendary loot only drops at those depths, every deep-tier item and all 10 weapon passives were unreachable content. Inner Core took the largest cut of any value in the project for that reason. See storm_timings.json _combined_note for the resulting per-layer totals.
depth_hazard._oxygen_removed: The five *_oxygen_drain keys were DELETED 2026-08-01 at the developer's request, together with DepthHazard._apply_oxygen_drain(). They were live (Mantle 1.5 / Outer Core 4.0 / Inner Core 8.0 stamina per second) but produced no visible feedback beyond a slightly shorter sprint. Do not re-add these keys without also restoring the code that reads them — an orphaned key here reads as live balance and will mislead the next tuning pass.
